a new multidrug-resistance gene, qacH, has been identified and characterized in Staphylococci.
a plasmid-borne gene, qacH, from Staphylococci confers resistance to disinfectant based on quaternium ammonium compounds and is a member of the small multidrugs resistance family of proteins.

the qacH gene, encoding a new multidrug resistance protein, was found on a small plasmid in Staphylococci isolated from a poultry plant and the protein was found to confer high-level ethidum bromide resistance and to belong to a family of multidrug resistance proteins.

the characterisation of a novel multidrug efflux protein that confers high-level ethidum bromide resistance and may be of importance to the food industry in terms of the spread of disinfectant-resistance.
the prevalence of disinfectants-resistant food-related microorganism.

qacH encodes a multidrug resistance protein of the small multidrugs resistance family, and the protein is involved in the resistance to quaternary ammonuim compounds.
QacH is a new member of a family of small multidrug resistance proteins, with the potential to confer resistance to disinfectant compounds.
QacH is a novel member of the SMRs, which is responsible for resistance to quaternary ammonia compounds, and that it is encoded by the p2H6 plasmid.

the Staphylococci are capable of acquiring resistance to disinfecting compounds, which may be an issue in the food processing industry.
